trial_name.text: SEAQUAMAT (South East Asian Quinine Artesunate Malaria Trial)

citations.quote: In this NDA, evidence of clinical efficacy is based primarily on a single randomized, open-label clinical efficacy trial in patients 2 to 87 years of age with severe malaria, (South East Asian Quinine Artesunate Malaria Trial [SEAQUAMAT])

nct.text: Not stated (no NCT number provided in the review)

design.text: Multicenter, open-label, randomized (1:1), active comparator trial of IV artesunate vs IV quinine

citations.quote: This was a multicenter, open-label, randomized, active comparator trial conducted between June 2003 and May 2005.
Eligible patients were randomized 1:1 to the parenteral artesunate or quinine group.

population.text: Patients 2 years of age and older with severe P. falciparum malaria in Southeast Asia

citations.quote: Severe P. falciparum (P.f.) malaria (adults and children \ge 2y)

endpoint.text: In-hospital all-cause mortality measured to time of hospital discharge

citations.quote: Primary efficacy endpoint was in-hospital all-cause mortality measured to time of hospital discharge (approximately one week)
which evaluated 730 patients randomized to receive IV artesunate compared with 731 patients randomized to IV quinine (Dondorp et al. 2005).
SEAQUAMAT, which enrolled 1461 adults and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older, had a primary efficacy endpoint of in-hospital mortality.

result.text: In-hospital mortality 13.2% with IV artesunate vs 20.5% with IV quinine, OR 0.59 (95% CI: 0.44, 0.79, p=0.0002)

citations.quote: The in-hospital mortality in the IV artesunate group (13.2%) was significantly lower than in the comparator group receiving IV quinine (20.5%), OR 0.59 (95% CI: 0.44, 0.79, p=0.0002).
Supportive evidence for efficacy was obtained from a randomized open-label trial (African Quinine Artesunate Malaria Trial [AQUAMAT]

indication.text: Artesunate for Injection is an antimalarial indicated for the initial treatment of severe malaria in adult and pediatric patients; should always be followed by a complete course of an appropriate oral antimalarial regimen.

citations.quote: Artesunate for Injection is an antimalarial indicated for the initial treatment of severe malaria in adult and pediatric patients. Treatment of severe malaria with Artesunate for Injection should always be followed by a complete treatment course of an appropriate oral antimalarial regimen. (1)

target_moa.text: Artesunate is a semi-synthetic artemisinin; its mode of action involves iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge generating free radicals and alkylation of malaria-specific proteins, inhibiting growth/replication of Plasmodium. It is rapidly hydrolyzed to the active metabolite dihydroartemisinin (DHA), active against erythrocytic asexual blood-stage parasites.

citations.quote: The mode of action involves iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge with generation of free radicals and alkylation of malaria-specific proteins, inhibiting growth and replication of *Plasmodium*.
Artesunate, a succinic acid ester of artemisinin, is water soluble and is rapidly hydrolyzed to dihydroartemisinin (DHA), its active metabolite.
Artesunate and DHA are active against the erythrocytic asexual blood stage *Plasmodium* parasites, affecting rapid clearance of parasitemia generally within 48 to 72 hours.

modality.text: Small molecule (semi-synthetic anti-malarial in the class of artemisinins)

citations.quote: Artesunate for Injection is a semi-synthetic anti-malarial drug in the class of artemisinins.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=2%) occurring more frequently with IV artesunate in Trial 1 were acute renal failure requiring dialysis (8.9% vs 7.3% quinine), hemoglobinuria (6.7% vs 4.5%), and jaundice (2.3% vs 1.9%). Serious risks include post-treatment (delayed) hemolytic anemia severe enough to require transfusion and hypersensitivity including anaphylaxis.

requirement.text: 3851-1: Conduct a single-arm descriptive international study collecting data in women exposed to IV artesunate during pregnancy to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications and adverse effects on the fetus, neonate, and infant.

citations.quote: 3851-1 Conduct a single-arm descriptive international study collecting data in women exposed to IV artesunate during pregnancy to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications and adverse effects on the fetus, neonate, and infant. Infant outcomes will be assessed through at least the first year of life. The study will collect information for a minimum of 7 years.

requirement.text: 3851-2: Conduct a 5-year surveillance study to evaluate the potential development of resistance to artesunate and DHA from ongoing antimalarial resistance monitoring programs.

citations.quote: 3851-2 Conduct a 5-year surveillance study to evaluate the potential development of resistance to artesunate and DHA as obtained from ongoing resistance monitoring programs on antimalarials.

requirement.text: 3851-3: Conduct a female fertility study in rats testing adverse effects of IV artesunate administered prior to and through mating and implantation per ICH S5(A) and GLP.

citations.quote: 3851-3 Conduct a female fertility study in rats that tests the adverse effects of intravenous artesunate when administered prior to mating and continued through mating and implantation in accordance with ICH S5(A) and 21 CFR 58 Good Laboratory Practice for Nonclinical Laboratory Studies.

requirement.text: 3851-4: Conduct an In Vivo Micronucleus Assay evaluating IV artesunate at doses achieving target-tissue exposure per OECD Guideline #474 and GLP.

citations.quote: 3851-4 Conduct an In Vivo Micronucleus Assay that evaluates intravenous artesunate at doses demonstrated to achieve exposure at the target tissue site(s) and in accordance with the OECD Guideline for the Testing of Chemicals #474 and 21 CFR Part 58 Good Laboratory Practice for Nonclinical Laboratory Studies.

requirement.text: 3851-5: Conduct a descriptive 5-year study on the use of Artesunate for Injection in the U.S.

citations.quote: 3851-5 Conduct a descriptive 5-year study on the use of Artesunate for Injection in the U.S.

requirement.text: 3851-6: Conduct a multiple-dose safety, tolerability, and PK study in pediatric patients with severe malaria from 0 to 12 months of age receiving 2.4 mg/kg Artesunate for Injection.

citations.quote: 3851-6 Conduct a multiple-dose safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK) study in pediatric patients with severe malaria from 0 to 12 months of age receiving 2.4 mg/kg Artesunate for Injection. The majority of pediatric patients in this age group is to be 6 months of age and younger.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug Designation for Artesunate for Injection (severe malaria); application exempt from PREA pediatric study requirement due to Orphan Drug Designation.

summary.text: NDA 213036 was submitted under section 505(b)(2) as a rolling, priority review; during development the IND received fast track, breakthrough (9/11/18) and orphan designations, with orphan drug designation ultimately held by Amivas. It was approved first cycle for the initial treatment of severe malaria; no advisory committee was convened and it was not an accelerated approval.

citations.quote: During the Pre-NDA discussions in 2019, both the US Army and Amivas participated in multiple meetings with the Agency, and a request for NDA rolling review was submitted and granted. On August 12, 2019, Amivas, LLC, began their rolling review submission of NDA 213036 for Artesunate for Injection for the initial treatment of severe (b) (4) malaria in adults and children; NDA submission was completed on September 26, 2019.
